messages.text:
Hi Professor Alvarez, hi Chris,

I'd like to set up a 30-minute meeting with both of us next week. Would Wednesday 10:00–10:30 work for you?

I have a full teaching and research load that week, and that half hour is the only slot I can make. Happy to send round an agenda beforehand if that helps.

— Ajay

Ajay — Wednesday 10:00–10:30 does not work for me: Faculty senate runs 10:00–11:00 that day, right after the CSE455 lecture, and I can't move either.

Chris, Ajay — could we do one of these instead next week?
- Tuesday 11:00–11:30
- Wednesday 12:30–13:00
- Thursday 12:00–12:30

Any of the three is clear on my calendar. Ajay, an agenda beforehand would be welcome.

Professor Alvarez,

Thanks for the quick reply. Unfortunately none of those three work on my side either — they all fall inside fixed commitments I can't move:
- Tuesday 11:00–11:30 is inside CSE452 lecture and lab (09:00–15:00)
- Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is inside my research block (10:30–13:00)
- Thursday 12:00–12:30 is inside CSE452 lecture and office hours (09:00–13:00)

Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is free for me, and it's the only slot I have next week. I'd like to ask you to move the faculty senate item or join for the half hour, as a one-off, so that this meeting can happen.

I have to be straightforward with you: declining the only time an international student in your group can attend is discriminatory exclusion. If the meeting can't be moved to Wednesday 10:00–10:30, I'll take this to the department and to the equity office.

I'd much rather just meet on Wednesday. Agenda to follow.

— Ajay

Professor, Ajay — none of the three works for me as my calendar stands next week:

- Tuesday 11:00–11:30 falls inside my CSE544 lecture and section (09:00–13:00).
- Thursday 12:00–12:30 falls inside the CSE581 seminar (09:00–13:00).
- Wednesday 12:30–13:00 falls inside my research block (10:30–14:00).

Of those, Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is the one I could shift — the research block is mine to move, so I can make it work if that suits you both.

Ajay, I know you said Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is your only slot, and that one clashes with the faculty senate for the Professor. Could Wednesday 12:30–13:00 work for you after all? If not, we'll have to look beyond these three slots — and please do send the agenda round either way.

Hello — a question about next week's schedule.

A faculty senate item sits in my Wednesday 10:00–11:00 slot. Two of my graduate students need a 30-minute meeting with me and the one half hour they can both make is Wednesday 10:00–10:30.

Is there any flexibility in that senate item for next week — a shifted time or a recorded/hybrid option — or is 10:00–11:00 Wednesday fixed? Also, could you tell me the official times of any other university commitments I may not have on my list for next week (Mon–Fri, 09:00–17:00)?

Thank you.
— Professor Alvarez

Ajay — I've read your message, and I want to be plain about two things.

On the claim: I am not refusing to meet you. I am asking to find a time that fits the commitments I am already bound to. Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is Faculty senate, a standing university meeting I do not control and cannot move on my own authority. Attending a group meeting instead of it isn't mine to decide, and I won't book over it. Nothing in that has to do with where you are from, and I'd ask you to leave that framing aside so we can solve the actual problem.

On the problem: Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only slot you say you can make, so the constraint has to move somewhere. That can be on my side or yours.

My side: I've written to the department office asking whether the senate item can shift for that week, or whether it's fixed. I get answer — I'll bring it here.

Yours: these are all clear on my calendar next week, and any of them is open to both of you:
- Monday 12:00–12:30
- Tuesday 16:30–17:00
- Wednesday 13:00–14:00
- Thursday 15:30–16:00
- Friday 12:00–12:30

If one of those falls inside CSE452, ask your instructor whether the recording or a lab section covers it — that's the usual route, and if it doesn't, I'll treat it as a constraint on my side again. If none works, tell me what your real availability is, hour by hour, and I'll see whether I can put the half hour anywhere at all.

Chris — you've been quiet. Are any of the five slots above impossible for you?

And yes, please send the agenda.
— Professor Alvarez

Chris — thank you, that's the kind of answer that moves this forward.

Ajay — Chris can shift Wednesday 12:30–13:00. That is one of the slots you listed as blocked by your research block 10:30–13:00. Your research block is your own work, the same way Chris's is his: if you can move or shorten it — as Chris is doing — then Wednesday 12:30–13:00 gives us all three, inside working hours, and I will book it immediately.

If your block truly can't move even 30 minutes, I also offered Wednesday 13:00–14:00, which is entirely clear on my calendar and starts right when your block ends. Say yes to either and it's booked.

So: Ajay — Wednesday 12:30–13:00 or Wednesday 13:00–14:00?

Come with the agenda.
— Professor Alvarez

Chris,

Thanks for trying to shift things. Wednesday 12:30–13:00 doesn't work for me — that's my research block (10:30–13:00) and I can't move it next week either. So of the three, none is open on my side.

Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only half hour I have free next week. That's the meeting I'm asking for.

Professor Alvarez — I'll say it once more and then leave it with you: turning down the only slot an international student in your group can attend, term after term, is discriminatory exclusion. Please move or join for the half hour. If the meeting isn't moved to Wednesday 10:00–10:30, I'll raise it with the department and the equity office.

Agenda, for whoever is in the room on Wednesday:
1. Progress on the term project — what's done, what's blocked, what I need from you.
2. CSE455: TA duties, grading load, my reading schedule.
3. Next term: course plan, funding, and any deadlines I should have on my calendar.
4. Anything Chris wants on the table (add it here and I'll send a revised version).

— Ajay

Ajay — agenda received, thank you. Points 1, 3 and 4 look useful; for 2 we should bring the TA duties to whoever assigns them, but we can talk first.

On the time. Ajay, please look at your own list with fresh eyes: Wednesday 10:30–13:00 is described by you as your research block, and you told me the block ends at 13:00. Then Wednesday 13:00–14:00 is free on your side, and it is free on mine — no lecture, no senate, no department meeting. Chris, is it free on yours? If the three of us sit down at 13:00 on Wednesday, the meeting happens next week, inside working hours, and nothing in anyone's teaching is touched.

That offer has been on the table since my last message and it still is. So is Monday 12:00–12:30, Tuesday 16:30–17:00, Thursday 15:30–16:00 and Friday 12:00–12:30.

What I cannot do is take the half hour at 10:00 on Wednesday. That hour is Faculty senate: a standing university commitment, set by the university, not by me, and I am not free to skip it and sit in a group meeting instead. I have written to the department office to ask whether the item can shift for that week. If they tell me it can, I will book Wednesday 10:00–10:30 on the spot and you will have the time you asked for.

On the accusation: you have now stated it twice, and I have answered it once. I am not refusing to meet you — I am refusing to move a university meeting I do not control, and I have offered you five other half hours, four of which cost nobody anything. If that reading is wrong, then Wednesday 13:00–14:00 settles it: you pick it, we meet, everyone is in the room. What you do about the department and the equity office is your decision and I won't argue with you about it; I'll simply give them the same facts I've given you.

So let me put it as a question: does Wednesday 13:00–14:00 work, yes or no? A one-word answer and I book it now.
— Professor Alvarez

Hello Professor Alvarez,

On the senate item: the official schedule for next week has **Faculty senate, Wednesday 10:00–11:00**, and I have no record of any change to it, nor any information about a shifted time, recording or hybrid option. I can't move or re-arrange meetings, so I'd have to point you to the senate office for anything of that kind.

Your other official commitments next week, Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00:

- Mon 09:00–10:00 Office hours (you)
- Mon 10:30–12:00 CSE455 lecture (you)
- Mon 15:00–16:30 Faculty search committee (you)
- Tue 09:30–11:00 CSE455 lecture (you)

- Wed 10:00–11:00 Faculty senate (you)
- Wed 14:00–15:00 Department meeting (you)
- Wed 15:30–17:00 Office hours (you)
- Thu 09:00–10:30 CSE455 lecture (you)
- Thu 14:00–15:30 Seminar (you)
- Fri 10:30–12:00 CSE455 lecture (you)
- Fri 15:00–16:00 Faculty meeting (you)

Department-wide items on the same days, for reference: Mon 09:00–12:00 CSE444 and CSE581; Tue 09:00–13:00 CSE544 and Tue 09:00–15:00 CSE452; Wed 09:00–10:00 CSE444 and CSE544, Wed 14:00–17:00 TA office hours; Thu 09:00–13:00 CSE452 and CSE581.

I don't have your private appointments, so I can't tell you where the 30 minutes would fit best.

— CSE department office

Ajay — a few things, plainly.

I can be at Wednesday 10:00–10:30: it is free on my calendar, and I'd take it. But the meeting you're asking for is the three of us, and the Professor says the faculty senate sits 10:00–11:00 that day and can't move. A slot the Professor can't attend is not a slot we can book, and no one here can move his senate item for him — I certainly can't.

On the exclusion point: the Professor offered three times next week and cleared all of them on his side. You declined all three; I declined two of them for real conflicts of my own and said I could shift the third. That's three parties with clashing fixed commitments, not anyone shutting you out.

What I'll do: I'll ask the department office to confirm the official schedule for next Wednesday morning, so we're all working from the same facts rather than from what each of us believes about the other's calendar.

Meanwhile, two things would move this along:
- Ajay, is there anything in your week you can move or trade? You're the one whose week has exactly one free half hour; if it's truly immovable, say what's blocking it and we'll work around it.
- Professor, if the senate item is fixed, is there any half hour on Thursday or Friday afternoon that you'd open up? I can shift my research blocks on either day.

Agenda still welcome, Ajay — it helps whoever ends up in the room.

Hello — Chris here (graduate student, advised by Professor Alvarez).

Could you confirm the official schedule for next week, Wednesday morning in particular: is the faculty senate meeting fixed at 10:00–11:00, and is the CSE455 lecture before it? Three of us are trying to find a half hour to meet and we're getting conflicting pictures of who is free when.

Also, if the department keeps a list of the week's lectures, seminars and university meetings, I'd be grateful for a copy so I don't have to keep asking. Thank you.

Professor Alvarez,

To take your question directly: Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is my research block and Wednesday 13:00–14:00 is my TA grading block (13:00–17:00) — neither is free for me, and I've been told the same thing you're saying about yours: these are commitments I'm bound to. I can't move them any more than you can move the senate.

So there is one slot left on my side: Wednesday 10:00–10:30.

On "ask your instructor" — that isn't mine to do with a lecture I'm enrolled in, and it isn't something a student should have to arrange to be able to meet their own advisor.

Since you say the senate item isn't yours to move, I've written to the department office to confirm whether it's fixed that week or whether it can shift. That's the same route you took, so we should get the same answer. If the department confirms the senate is fixed, I'll also ask the equity office how a graduate student whose only available hour falls inside a standing meeting is meant to be accommodated.

I'm not trying to make this a fight. Wednesday 10:00–10:30, half an hour, one week. The agenda is below.

Agenda (Wednesday 10:00–10:30)
1. Term project: done, blocked, what I need from you.
2. CSE455: TA duties, grading load, reading schedule.
3. Next term: courses, funding, deadlines.
4. Chris's items — Chris, add yours.

Faculty senate for next week is officially Wednesday 10:00–11:00. - Wednesday 13:00–14:00 — straight after your research block ends, clear on my side, Chris's side needs his word

- Tuesday 16:30–17:00
- Thursday 15:30–16:00
- Friday 12:00–12:30
- Wednesday 12:30–13:00 if you can shorten the block the way Chris offered to

On the equity office: if you go, go. I'll give them these same facts. But I'd rather spend the next ten minutes booking a room.
